author: Rory Robinson
title: NBA fans cry 'rigged' after massive foul not called in Pistons-Cavaliers Game 5 - NewsBreak
text:
By Rory Robinson ,
40 minutes ago The NBA is doing itself no favors by sidestepping conspiracy theories about predetermined scripts and outcomes after a contentious no-call at the end of regulation in the Detroit Pistons and Cleveland Cavaliers Game 5 playoff matchup.
NBA fans brought out "rigged" accusations across the internet on Wednesday night just before the Cavaliers escaped with a 117-113 overtime win and took a 3-2 series lead in the Eastern Conference semifinals.
All eyes were on the final play of regulation when officials let Jarrett Allen off the hook for what appeared to be a clear foul on Ausar Thompson with about a second left. The hoops world started the day amped after ESPN's First Take kicked off the morning by yelling about Philadelphia's sports culture .

• Stephen A Smith finds himself in shouting match live on ESPN as tensions boil over
With the clock winding down, Donovan Mitchell brought the ball up against tight defense from Thompson. Evan Mobley then set a sturdy screen to draw Cade Cunningham into a double-team.
Mitchell attacked downhill after turning the corner and appeared ready to loft a short floater inside the lane. Thompson recovered from behind and blocked the shot attempt cleanly in one of the defining defensive plays of the game.
As the ball bounced free near the buzzer, Allen crashed into Thompson going for the loose ball. Thompson hit the floor as the clock hit zero, but the refs kept their whistles silent.
Pistons fans were furious as a foul call would have put Thompson at the line with just over a second left and a real shot to win it before overtime. Now Detroit heads to Cleveland for a must-win on Friday, still frustrated that Game 5 slipped away before overtime even started.
Instead, the Cavaliers survived and eventually closed out the game in overtime behind Mitchell and James Harden, who combined for 51 points. "How is that not a foul??? Clear trip. Crooked NBA. Rigged," one fan posted.
Another compared the moment to the infamous 2002 Lakers-Kings playoff controversy, writing: "Two games in my life I’m convinced the NBA rigged. This one. And Lakers-Kings Game 6."
Some fans even joked about calling it the 'WWENBA' because the ending felt so scripted.
The no-call ended up stealing the spotlight from some huge performances on the court. Cunningham delivered a 39-point, nine-assist performance while Harden nearly finished with a triple-double after pouring in 30 points, eight rebounds, and six assists.
Detroit led most of the way, holding the advantage for nearly 70 percent of the game. But Cleveland's experience, free throws and that missed call flipped the momentum late.
The NBA was already fighting allegations of poor officiating from top players before the game including Boston Celtics star Jaylen Brown. The Celtics wing was fined $50,000 for publicly criticizing referees after a first-round exit from the 76ers.
